text: The average carbon footprint in France was about 9.2 t CO2e per person in 2022, while a 1.5–2 °C world needs about 2 t by 2050.
source: SDES, Ministry for the Ecological Transition (2023); Selectra

text: Realistic everyday changes (less meat, fewer flights, better insulation) can cut a French footprint by about a quarter; the rest depends on companies and public policy.
Digital technology accounts for about 4.4% of France's carbon footprint once data centres abroad are counted.
Around 80% of a device's carbon footprint comes from making it, not from using it, so keeping a phone longer is the biggest digital lever.
Choosing a refurbished smartphone instead of a new one avoids most of its manufacturing emissions and raw materials.
Making a single smartphone moves roughly 200 kg of raw materials; a laptop, several hundred kilos.
In France, an hour of video streaming emits on the order of 64 g CO2e, small per hour but large across billions of hours.
A video watched 1 million times a day for five minutes adds up to roughly 1,900 t CO2e of streaming a year.
source: Design estimate from the Impact CO2 (ADEME) video factor

text: Deleting old emails and cloud photos saves almost nothing compared with keeping your devices longer or skipping one flight.
Data centres used about 415 TWh of electricity in 2024, around 1.5% of the world's total, and could more than double by 2030.
A typical AI text answer uses a few watt-hours at most, while generating a six-second AI video can take around 115 Wh.
One major AI provider measured its median text prompt at 0.24 Wh, about the energy of nine seconds of television.
source: Google technical paper on AI inference footprint (August 2025)

text: Training one frontier language model of the 2023 generation was estimated at around 42 GWh of electricity.
Widespread use of existing AI applications could cut around 5% of energy-related emissions by 2035, more than data centres add.
France's AFNOR Spec 2314 defines frugal AI: first question the need, then prefer smaller models, then measure and disclose the impact.
A return flight Paris–New York emits about 1.8 t CO2e per passenger, close to a whole year of a 2-tonne lifestyle.
Paris–Singapore and back emits about 3.2 t CO2e per passenger, more than a year and a half of a 2-tonne lifestyle.
One long-haul return flight often weighs more than a whole year of a sustainable 2-tonne footprint.
Taking the train from Paris to London, Milan or Rotterdam emits a small fraction of the same trip by plane, often less than a tenth.
About 1% of the world's population causes more than half of the emissions from passenger air travel.
Warming rises almost linearly with cumulative CO2: every 1,000 Gt of CO2 emitted adds about 0.45 °C.
source: IPCC AR6 WG1, Summary for Policymakers (2021)

text: Current climate policies put the world on track for roughly 2.7 °C of warming by 2100.
source: Climate Action Tracker; IPCC AR6 scenario range

text: 2024 was the first calendar year about 1.55 °C warmer than pre-industrial times.
source: WMO, State of the Global Climate 2024 (2025)

text: By 2100, median sea-level rise is about 0.38 m in the lowest-emission scenario and about 0.77 m in the highest.
At 1.5 °C about 6% of insect species lose more than half their range; at 2 °C it is 18%, and at 3.2 °C almost half.
At 2.7 °C of warming, about 2 billion people would live outside the climate niche humans have thrived in for millennia.
The August 2003 heatwave caused around 15,000 excess deaths in France, most of them people over 75.
Teens who spend more than three hours a day on social media face double the risk of depression and anxiety symptoms.
source: US Surgeon General, Advisory on Social Media and Youth Mental Health (2023)

text: In a large experiment, people who deactivated a major social network for four weeks felt happier and gained about an hour a day.
source: Allcott et al., American Economic Review (2020)

text: The average internet user spends about 2 h 21 min a day on social media.
Working 55 hours or more a week is linked to a 35% higher risk of stroke and a 17% higher risk of dying from heart disease.
The WHO classifies burnout as an occupational phenomenon caused by chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed.
In a 2022 UK trial of the four-day week, 56 of 61 companies kept it afterwards and most staff reported less burnout.
source: Autonomy / Schor et al., UK four-day week pilot results (2023)

text: Strong social relationships raise the odds of survival by about 50%, an effect comparable to quitting smoking.
About 60% of jobs in advanced economies are exposed to AI; roughly half could benefit, the other half could see lower demand.
source: IMF, Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work (2024)

text: Life expectancy at birth in France is about 85.9 years for women and 80.3 years for men.
Over a 13-year life, a 15 kg dog's footprint was estimated at about 8.2 t CO2e, mostly from its food; a cat's is smaller.
A large superyacht can burn enough fuel to emit thousands of tonnes of CO2 a year, more than hundreds of French households combined.
source: Barros & Wilk, Sustainability: Science, Practice and Policy (2021)

text: Rocket soot released high in the atmosphere warms about 500 times more than the same soot from planes or cars.
The largest cryptocurrency network uses roughly as much electricity per year as a mid-sized European country.
